definition: Penalties added to the loss on parameter magnitudes.
details: Penalties added to the loss on parameter magnitudes. L1 pushes weights to exactly zero (sparsity); L2, implemented as weight decay in optimizers like AdamW, shrinks weights smoothly and is standard in transformer training.

explainer.lead: L2 regularization adds a penalty on squared parameter magnitudes to the loss, shrinking weights smoothly. It is standard in transformer training, implemented as weight decay in optimizers like AdamW.

tiers.eli5: It's a gentle pull that keeps every knob small, so the model doesn't overreact to any single input.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers use it as a default regularizer, usually through weight decay in AdamW. Unlike L1, it does not push weights to exactly zero, so it does not produce sparsity.
tiers.paperLevel: A penalty proportional to the sum of squared parameter values is added to the loss, shrinking weights smoothly. It is contrasted with L1, which drives weights to exactly zero.

explainer.example: In transformer training, weight decay in AdamW applies an L2-style shrinkage to weights each step.
